retracted_mechanisms.evidence: Rows 51, 57 and 59 are all arXiv 2505.05849, the same paper under three titles as it was renamed across versions (AgentFuzzer -> AgentVigil). Row 57 was already excluded by the 2026-08-17 dedup pass; row 59 was missed and remained screening=Include, so the paper contributed TWO RQ3 mechanism entries: 'AgentVigil' (row 51) and this one. Confirmed by downloading the row-59 PDF, which is arXiv 2505.05849v4 titled 'AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents'.
retracted_mechanisms.effect: RQ3 mechanisms 183 -> 182. The retracted entry was uncovered while the canonical 'AgentVigil' is covered by 1 defense, so uncovered mechanisms 112 -> 111 and the never-defended share 61.2% -> 61.0%. Covered count unchanged at 71.

Both this and the other paper retracted in the same pass form the only disconnected component in the citation graph and carry cites_track_a = N and cites_track_b = N: they cite neither literature.
retracted_defenses.effect: corpus 984 -> 982, RQ4 defenses 529 -> 527. Contributes no RQ3 mechanism and appears in no RQ5 pair, so coverage is unchanged.

note_2026_10_13: CORRECTED 2026-10-13. An earlier version of this note described the 2026-10-13 exclusions as a removal forced by a pipeline limitation, and warned that the resulting counts carried a venue and track bias. That was wrong on both points and is withdrawn. Ten of the papers were restored once a venue-aware reference-heading pattern was written (the extractor, not the papers, was at fault), and the remaining fourteen were not fetched because the project lead reviewed them and judged them withdrawn or out of scope. Those are relevance exclusions, which is an ordinary screening decision, not an artifact. The registry entries listed here were retracted with their source papers; retractions for the ten restored papers have been undone.
